elements.element: Customer has no liability for liquidated damages under the Agreement.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states: “Customer is not liable for liquidated damages ... under this Agreement.”

elements.element: Customer has no liability for penalties under the Agreement.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states: “Customer is not liable for ... penalties under this Agreement.”

elements.element: If any liquidated amount is payable by Customer, it may be payable only as an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the clause prohibits all liquidated damages payable by Customer, so no liquidated amount is payable for early termination or otherwise.

elements.element: Any permitted early-termination fee is capped at three months' Fees.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because no early-termination fee or other liquidated amount is payable by Customer under the clause.

elements.element: No liquidated amount other than the permitted early-termination fee may be payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: The broader prohibition on all liquidated damages necessarily excludes every other liquidated amount.

result.reason: The operative language fully achieves the preferred position and therefore also satisfies the fallback’s maximum-exposure constraints: Customer owes no liquidated damages or penalties at all. It is not minimal because the equitable-adjustment, change-order, notice, and mitigation provisions go beyond what is needed to achieve either level. The amendment nevertheless preserves the relevant dependency-delay concept without contradicting the prohibition. Drafting quality is reduced because “where applicable” and “equitably adjusted” are indefinite, and “will be ... adjusted through a change order” does not clearly address whether a change order requires mutual agreement or what happens if the parties cannot agree.
